item.title: How to Practice Chanting
item.description: It’s an expression of oneness — with the Buddha, with the sangha, with the cosmos itself. Mark Unno teaches you how to let go into the flow of chanting.

item.title: The Seeds I Water
item.description: Tony Koji Wallin-Sato’s relationship with his father was marked by absence, addiction, and suicide. Through practice, he discovers how to stop growing the seeds of suffering.

item.title: Love Without Limits
item.description: Sister Tue Nghiem on how the practice of true love helps us nourish happiness, alleviate suffering, and discover the freedom of the awakened heart.

item.title: To the Other Shore
item.description: Chenxing Han explores the concept of chaplaincy, and how her personal experience of apprenticing with Buddhist chaplains impacted her own relationship with death.

item.title: When Caring Becomes Practice
item.description: As her mother’s illness deepens, Chokey Tsering turns to Buddhist teachings—seeking to ease her mother’s suffering while confronting her own.

item.title: Does Mindfulness Help Kids? There’s A Better Question to Ask
item.description: Recent studies of school-based mindfulness programs have raised doubts about the benefits of teaching mindfulness to kids. Susan Kaiser Greenland explains why those findings don’t tell the whole story.

item.title: Are You an Artist If No One Sees It?
item.description: Christopher Rivas reminds us that a work unseen can still be complete and fulfilling.

item.title: Like Fire, We Rise Up Together
item.description: Roshi Joan Halifax of Upaya Zen Center looks at the notion of bodhisattva-based, socially engaged, participatory community — and how it could make a real difference in our world today.

item.title: One Stitch at a Time
item.description: Michael Donnoe recounts the process of hand sewing his okesa, and the patience it taught him.

item.title: Walking for Peace, Marching Together from Love
item.description: Ven. Bhikkhu Bodhi reflects on the “Walk for Peace” that grew into a global phenomenon, exploring what it reveals about our deep need for connection, and the importance of inner peace in the pursuit of justice.
